title: DeepSeek Search 401 with a chat proxy: separate tool credentials and endpoints
h1: DeepSeek Search 401 with a chat proxy: separate tool credentials and endpoints
description: Diagnose DeepSeek search authentication failures when chat through a gateway works. Separate tool origins, key issuers, partial upstream fixes and Search/Fetch billing.
summary: A working chat route does not validate the credential for a separate search service. Bind each tool to its intended origin and credential issuer before retrying or enabling automatic search.

caseStudy.linkLabel: DeepSeek Search 401 with a chat proxy: separate tool credentials and endpoints

evidence.excerpt: It reads `$DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL`, independently of the conversation adapter’s `$DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`.

401 | The API key is missing or invalid.
Search | Per 1,000 successful requests | $0.75
fix(deepseek): keep a chat proxy's model key away from DeepSeek search and balance

verification.note: Reviewed official DeepSeek documentation and Harness source, plus OpenClaw issue, patch and release metadata on 2026-10-27. No model, Search or Fetch request, credential creation or paid call was executed.

review.distinctProblem: deepseek-chat-proxy-key-search-origin-mismatch; independent of existing pagination, feed entitlement and model-output cases.

sections.symptoms: [Harness discussion #408](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/408) and [OpenClaw issue #183830](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/183830) describe a gateway-backed chat route working while search authentication fails. These separate reports support an integration failure pattern, not a measured failure rate or proof that every gateway is affected.
sections.cause: The [pinned Harness module](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/22ddee3792402c3e70ec5f86a63c3e3e895a2f60/packages/web/web-search-deepseek/README.md) configures its auxiliary Messages-based search endpoint separately from chat. Its readiness check cannot prove a key is valid or the endpoint supports the required search tool. Do not confuse this model-turn search backend with the [dedicated Search/Fetch module](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/22ddee3792402c3e70ec5f86a63c3e3e895a2f60/packages/web/web-deepseek-api/README.md): the latter uses retrieval endpoints. A proxy-issued chat key sent to the official search service can produce 401.
sections.verification:
Reviewed official DeepSeek documentation and Harness source, plus OpenClaw issue, patch and release metadata on 2026-10-27. No model, Search or Fetch request, credential creation or paid call was executed.

Proposed controls: an official-origin route with the appropriate key, a proxy route that must not inherit an official tool credential, a missing key, and a deliberately mismatched issuer/origin. Inspect the resolved host and error classification without exposing headers. None of these network controls was executed here. Upstream tests and repository build checks do not establish live authentication success.
sections.limitations:
The [official tool guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search/#billing) prices Search and Fetch separately at US$0.75 per 1,000 successful requests. Charging requires HTTP 200 plus nonempty results/content; unsuccessful or empty retrievals are not billed. The described DeepSeek-backed server tools used through Harness, Claude Code or Codex begin per-request billing on November 1, 2026 at 00:00 Beijing time (01:00 KST). This is not a price change for every call made by those products. Track tool requests separately from model tokens, especially for the Messages-based search backend.

No actual Search API usage volume, all-proxy compatibility or fixed-release runtime was established. The new [DeepSeek profile](../../apis/deepseek/) deliberately covers Search/Fetch rather than an unverified full model catalog. Search terms are candidates, not measured demand; no GetBeta resolution of this exact problem was verified.
